r0.why: Bayes' theorem to give and update hypothesis probability (1), prior to posterior (2), important in (mathematical) statistics (3).

r1.why: Dynamic analysis of data sequences (4), listed fields (5), tied to subjective/Bayesian probability in decision theory (6).

r2.why: H and E definitions (7,10), competing hypotheses (8), prior (9), posterior is what we want (11,12).

r3.why: Likelihood and compatibility (13,14), marginal likelihood (16), P(E)>0 (18), same for all hypotheses so no effect on relative probabilities (17).

r4.why: Only prior and likelihood affect posterior, proportional to inherent likeliness and fit to evidence (19).

r5.why: Procedure repeated on new evidence (39), models with degrees of belief (36,38), parameterization updates all in one step (40), belief over parameter space (41).

r6.why: Widely used and computationally convenient (24), not only rational rule (25), Hacking on Dutch books (26), non-Bayesian rules avoiding Dutch books after Jeffrey's rule (30,31).
